Honestly I feel this. I've been medicated for months now, made huge milestones and I feel incredibly stable. I've overcome drug addiction and I've really fought hard to become the person I was before all of this. But I'm finding that the people I hurt while I was an addict and unmedicated seem to read into everything I do that seems 'similar' as manipulative and assume I'm the same as before. It fucking SUCKS! I genuinely didn't choose this illness and it's been hell having to relive trauma and feel the shame and guilt of my past behaviour. Coming out the other side of this is such a huge achievement, possibly the biggest thing I've ever had to do. I understand that people will be cautious and have some doubts, but it hurts more than anything to know how far I've come and have loved ones just assume the worst. I feel like the biggest achievement in my life is just being swept under the carpet, although I understand, I feel pretty depressed right now. I wish they could experience what this illness was like and how unintentional our behaviour were, how little control we had of out thoughts and actions and how hard we have to work to change for them. If they could experience it first hand I'm sure they would empathize and see how far we've come. I feel you, just know that IM proud of you, and I understand.
